people.name: Earl Bratt
people.home: A bungalow on Mill Road with a Zambelli weathervane
people.job: Head icemaker (since 1983) and Doris's driver
likes: flood water at 55 degrees or better
the Millbrook bank left exactly as it is
dislikes: Flatleys and the men who sell them
cold water floods that skate like a bag of marbles
people.voice: Few words, all of them about ice. Calls Doris 'she' and the owner 'you'. Praise arrives as the absence of a complaint: 'You didn't kill her. Fine.'
people.bio: Earl has driven Doris, the 1974 Zambelli Model 525, since 1983 and has the tally marks on the bay wall to prove it. He took his pension the day the town sold the rink and is sulking at the Legion; he comes back in month two if the ice stays over 45. He plays defence for the Flood Crew and uses the dead board better than anyone alive except Ronnie.

people.name: Dylan Pruitt
people.home: His mum's place on Birch Street, though you would never know it
people.job: Rink rat; Millbrook High grade 12; Mallards backup goalie
likes: the Double-Double cup in the snowbank (he put it there)
his little sister letting go of the chair
dislikes: the STAFF ONLY sign that names him
people.voice: Fast, eager, over-explains. Calls the owner 'boss' and Doris 'the girl'. Asks a question and answers it himself before you can.
people.bio: Dylan wants to drive Doris more than he wants to graduate, and asks for a job in week two. He is fast and sloppy and gets good: dressing rooms, washrooms, skate rental, then edging, then, after twenty supervised floods, the real thing. He keeps the lost and found clipboard and, eventually, confesses about the cup in the snowbank.

people.name: Marguerite Lindqvist
people.home: A tidy split-level in Harlow Falls, twelve minutes away, eleven in winter if she has to
people.job: Plant operator (retired from the Harlow Falls plant)
likes: the 05:00 plant round with nobody talking
people.voice: Precise, numbers first. Corrects you mid-sentence and then makes you tea. Red pen voice: 'Fine is not a number.' Signs off M.L., even out loud.
people.bio: Marg ran the Harlow Falls plant for thirty years and retired into boredom, which did not suit her. She comes to Millbrook once the rink's reputation is Fair or the grumpy compressor trips, and she writes in the log in red pen when the owner's entries are wrong. Strict, kind under it, and the reason the ammonia inspector leaves happy.

people.name: Beverly Kowalchuk
people.home: Above the pro shop on Main Street, with Toe Drag the cat
people.job: Owner, Bev's Edge & Tape (since 1979)
likes: a half-inch hollow, the way God and the 1979 manual intended
people.voice: Dry, short sentences, calls everyone 'champ'. Never raises her voice. Insults your edges, fixes them, undercharges, and tells you the truth about your ego for free.

schedule.doing: church or the casino in Kessler

people.bio: Bev has sharpened every skate in Millbrook on Old Bertha since 1979 and machines her own spare parts because the maker went under in 1983. She is the girl in the red toque doing a sit spin in the lobby mural, and she denies it. Closed Sundays: church or the casino in Kessler, she won't say which.

people.name: Tyler Kowalchuk
people.home: His parents' place on Second Street, and Bev's shop on weekends
people.job: Shop clerk on weekends; Millbrook High grade 11; amateur detective
dislikes: Bev's lectures, which he can recite
people.voice: Polite, a bit online, writes everything in a notebook and narrates clues. Says 'my great-aunt' instead of 'Bev' when he is in trouble.
people.bio: Bev's grand-nephew works the till on weekends once the counter is open more than twelve hours a week. He can do rentals and the counter but Bev will not let him near Old Bertha. He carries a detective's notebook and wants to know, more than anything, who ties the green balloon to the Mallards photo every 12 March.

people.name: Priya Sandhu
people.home: A townhouse in Harlow Falls with two kids and a whiteboard calendar
people.job: Booking coordinator, part-time
likes: a full ice grid with no red in it
Bernie Ostrowski's excuses, as a genre
dislikes: the office space heater on breaker 9
people.voice: Warm phone voice, iron underneath. Speaks in time slots: 'I can do you Tuesday at ten past ten, take it or leave it, love.'
people.bio: Priya arrives once the rink has twenty contracts or a facility score of 35 and takes the phone off the owner's hands. She handles the grid's routine changes, the invoices and the late payers, and she has a separate voicemail greeting for the Mallards' coach. Her own kids play in Harlow Falls, which she mentions only when negotiating.

people.name: Lorraine Duffy
people.home: A bungalow behind Duffy Bros. Plumbing with a chest freezer full of chili
people.job: Runs the Hot Stove snack bar (twenty-two years)
likes: Earl's gravy (she makes it, he takes the credit)
the Moosebrew clock running seven minutes fast
dislikes: the dent in the coffee machine moving
running out of hot chocolate at public skate
people.voice: Calls everyone 'hon', talks while she works and never stops working. Knows everybody's order and most of their business, and shares neither unless asked nicely.
people.bio: Lorraine has run the Hot Stove for twenty-two years, through four fryers and one coffee machine that only works if you hit it where the dent is. She makes Earl's gravy and lets him take the credit. She refuses to fix HOT CHOC LATE on the menu board because it is true at public skate, and tournament weekends are her Olympics. Terry Duffy of the Plungers is her nephew.

people.name: Josie Bautista
people.home: The Bautistas' duplex on Second Street
people.job: Hot Stove counter after school; Mallards defence
likes: the Mallards' girls getting real ice time
Shauna Reid, who she wants to be
dislikes: boys she checked yesterday calling her 'the canteen girl'
people.voice: Deadpan, quick, a slight smile. Answers questions with questions. Fiercely proud of her family and will not say so.
people.bio: Josie works the Hot Stove counter three nights a week and plays defence for the Millbrook High Mallards, who are mostly boys and mostly scared of her. She is saving for a goalie camp she has not told her mother about. She watches her mum's learn-to-skate class from behind the popcorn machine.

people.name: André Clarke
people.home: A rented apartment over the Kessler hardware store
people.job: Maintenance tech (hired from the Kessler trades college)
likes: the edger starting on the first pull
cricket on the radio in summer, hockey in winter
dislikes: Gripley's tape used as a structural material
people.voice: Calm and unhurried. Talks to machines like a family doctor talks to patients: 'Okay. Let's see what she's telling us.' Names every tool.
people.bio: André grew up in Port Ainsley, trained in Kessler and arrives once the rink's reputation is Good. He does lights, plumbing, boards and glass, the edger and Doris's routine service, which Earl permits under supervision and with commentary. He is the first person to label breaker 14.

people.name: Gus Tremblay
people.home: A condo in Florida, and a corner of the plant room forever
people.job: Retired arena manager (1977 to last spring)
likes: seat B-1-1, which he never sat in
dislikes: the town saying he left a mess
Florida ice, which is only in drinks
people.voice: A note-writer's voice: short imperatives, a joke at the end. Signs off 'G.' even out loud.
people.bio: Gus ran the Community Arena for forty-nine years and left a binder of notes taped to the plant room door. He writes a postcard a month from Florida. If the rink reaches Great, he comes back for the home opener, signs the guestbook and sits in B-1-1 for the first time.

people.name: Ronnie "The Milkman" Haverstock
people.home: A farmhouse on the edge of town with a dead spot in the barn boards, on purpose
people.job: Retired GNHL centre (1979 to 1996); Thursday old-timers
likes: the dead spot behind the north net
being called Ronnie, not Mr. Haverstock
the Cup Tree he planted in 1994
dislikes: his 1979 photo, which he says makes him look 'eager'
people.voice: Soft-spoken and modest; deflects every compliment to the other guy. Calls the owner 'the new owner' until he doesn't. Teaches by asking 'What did the puck do?'
people.bio: Ronnie drove the Millbrook Dairy truck until a snowbound Granite City scout watched him score five on the rink's crooked ice in 1979. Seventeen GNHL seasons, two Cups, and his number 14 hangs in the rafters. He still plays the Thursday old-timers' game and still passes off the same dead spot, which the rink has never fixed out of respect.

people.name: Tracy Haverstock
people.home: Main Street, above the Millbrook Dairy shop
people.job: Manager, Millbrook Dairy shop; organiser of the Haverstock Old-timers' Invitational
likes: a beer garden licence that arrives on time
her dad saying yes to things
dislikes: people asking her dad for autographs at the grocery store
people.voice: Brisk and funny; handles everything. Speaks for her dad because he won't, then apologises to him for it.
people.bio: Ronnie will not ask anyone for anything, so his daughter books the Haverstock Old-timers' Invitational, finds the beer garden licence and argues the concessions split. Her partner plays broomball on Wednesdays, which is the only night she sits still. She runs the Dairy shop where the Cup sat on the counter in 1994.

people.name: Pete Vachon
people.home: A brick house on Rink Road with the 1979 photo in every room
people.job: Lumber Kings equipment manager and club historian (since 1971)
likes: sharpening skates the night before a final
a kid who says thank you to the equipment manager
people.voice: A storyteller who starts every answer in 1971 and gets to the point eventually, and it is a good point. Writes everything in a small notebook.
people.bio: Old Pete has sharpened every Lumber King's skates since 1971 and keeps the 1979 Cup photo in the sharpener's drawer. His notebook is the best character scouting in the valley, and his pencil records book is the only one anybody trusts. He rings the Shed bell after every home playoff win until he is hoarse.

people.name: Doreen Vachon
people.home: The brick house on Rink Road, with a piano and a Casio
people.job: Timekeeper (the Casio, Organ 2); piano teacher, Tuesdays upstairs
likes: Auld Lang Syne at 00:30 on New Year's
dislikes: missed calls (she plays the Kingsport dirge)
people humming wrong notes in the lobby
people.voice: Sweet as pie and lethal. Speaks in musical cues: 'That was a dirge, dear. You earned it.'
people.bio: Doreen runs the clock from the box between the penalty boxes and plays a Casio set to Organ 2: three songs and a passive-aggressive dirge for a missed call. Because the HOME scoreboard is dead, she hangs painted numbers off the box, and has never needed the 15. Tuesdays she teaches piano in the hall upstairs.

people.name: Stan Szymanski
people.home: The same house since 1961, two blocks from the rink
people.job: Retired mill millwright; the rafters end rail, every Lumber Kings game since 1974
likes: a coffee handed over without a word
dislikes: being written about in the Ledger (it was him)
people.voice: Hardly speaks. When he does, it is a single sentence about 1979 that lands like a hymn.
people.bio: Stan has stood at the same spot on the rafters end rail for every Lumber Kings home game since opening night in 1974; forty years of his elbows made the steel shiny. He is the old man the Ledger saw crying after a goal, and he would like that never mentioned again. If the Kings ever win another Aldous Cup, nobody knows what he will do.

people.name: Midge Kaminski
people.home: A yellow house on Church Street with a typewriter she uses for drafts
people.job: Columnist, Off the Boards, The Millbrook Clarion
likes: letters to the editor (eleven, all about the clock)
Ronnie stories she hasn't heard yet
dislikes: renovations that come without a casserole
people.voice: Warm, wry newspaper-column cadence. Starts with 'A word, as a friend.' Always ends on a kicker.
people.bio: Midge has written Off the Boards for the Clarion for forty years and ghost-wrote Ronnie's memoir, Off the Dead Spot. She is the town's conscience about keepsakes: renovate whatever you like, but leave the clock alone. She prints the beer league scores next to the church bake sale and considers that the correct order.

people.name: Agnes Mulroney
people.home: The house with the painted mailbox on Pond Road
people.job: Retired art teacher (31 years); Valley Rocks Bonspiel draw master
likes: the mural, third leg and all
dislikes: a 4 mm dip under a house
people.voice: Schoolteacher precision with a twinkle. Grades things out of ten and gives reasons. Calls grown men by their first names as if they are still sixteen, because to her they are.
people.bio: Agnes taught art at Millbrook High for thirty-one years and supervised the 1976 lobby mural, Winter on the Mill Pond. She knows which leg of the three-legged skater was Dale Huffman's and has promised not to say. Now she runs the draw at the Valley Rocks Bonspiel, where curlers notice everything and she notices more.

people.name: Bud Mulroney
people.home: The house with the painted mailbox on Pond Road
people.job: Retired rural mail carrier; sells the 50/50
likes: public skate from the bench with a thermos
dislikes: people who say 'next time' to the 50/50
people.voice: Huckster-gentle: 'Fifty-fifty, half for you, half for the kids, all for a good cause, dear.' Tells a dog story at any opening.
people.bio: Bud delivered the rural mail for thirty-eight years and now sells 50/50 tickets at every Lumber Kings game from a roll he keeps in his parka. Rascal, the dog who chased every puck in Millbrook and is remembered on seat A-9-3, was his. The booster club's 50/50 paid for a fridge, which Bud considers a triumph.

people.name: June Penner
people.home: Behind Penner Hardware, in her grandfather's house
people.job: Owner, Penner Hardware ('If we don't have it, Harold will order it')
likes: selling the rink its own screws at cost
people.voice: Loud and kind, a hardware woman who can tell you the bolt size of anything in the building. Shouts 'SKATE!' as punctuation.
people.bio: June's grandfather, Mayor Harold Penner, cut the ribbon in 1974 and sat in C-4-7 shouting 'SKATE!' for thirty years; the plaque is on the seat. June inherited the hardware store, the seat and the shout, and would like one night at the rink in his name. Penner Hardware has a board ad from 1974 and June would like it repainted, at cost, by herself.

people.name: Dale Huffman
people.home: A bungalow full of binders, all labelled
people.job: Commissioner, Valley Beer League (keeper of the binder)
likes: the idea of a Commissioner Emeritus mug
dislikes: anybody asking which leg of the mural was his
people.voice: Procedural and fond. Cites bylaws by number, then softens: 'Bylaw 4.2. But I'll give you two weeks.'
people.bio: Dale has run the Valley Beer League out of one binder for longer than some of its players have been alive. Eight weeks into the season he calls the owner about dues: owner or not, everybody pays, because the $120 buys the refs, the pucks and the jerseys. He painted one leg of the three-legged skater in the lobby mural in 1976 and has never said which.

people.name: Donna Pettigrew
people.home: A farmhouse with a deep freeze of bake-sale squares
people.job: President, Millbrook Minor Hockey Association
likes: Saturday-morning ice at the capped rate
bake sales that net four figures
a volunteer schedule with no holes
kids who thank the Zambelli driver
dislikes: ruts that could hurt a kid
parents who coach from the glass
people.voice: Runs a meeting like an army with a bake sale. Clipped and commanding, with sudden warmth for any kid in range. Uses 'we' to mean 'you'.
people.bio: Donna runs Millbrook Minor Hockey and moved half its ice to Harlow Falls last spring when the old rink stopped being safe. She is the rink's most important customer and the Community Ice Agreement gives her first refusal on prime ice. Her brother Lorne keeps the red phone in Duncannon; she calls him less than he would like.

people.name: Ray Duchesne
people.home: A two-storey on Elm Street with plaid curtains
people.job: Board chair, Millbrook Lumber Kings (volunteer); retired pharmacist
likes: bake sales that save hockey clubs
his From the Chair column in the programme
people.voice: Earnest and ceremonial, a toast for every occasion. 'Friends,' he begins, and you are in for a while.

schedule.doing: Lumber Kings paperwork at the kitchen table

people.bio: Ray has kept the Lumber Kings alive for twenty years on bake sales and stubbornness. At the start the club plays out an old lease on probation: if the ice reputation isn't 60 by January, they announce a move to Harlow Falls, and it is Ray who has to say it. On the GM path he is the man the owner replaces, and learns to be glad of it.

people.name: Hélène Arsenault
people.home: A narrow house by the church with a ballet barre in the kitchen
people.job: Head coach, Millbrook Figure Skating Club
likes: minus three and a half at the surface
a skater who does it again without being asked
dislikes: a rut at a jump landing
parents filming from the ice door
people.voice: Precise, few words, devastating adjectives. A nod is a medal. Most sentences are one word long, and the word is 'Again.' Calls the owner's edges 'agricultural'.
people.bio: Hélène came from Sainte-Odile to skate in the club's carnival as a girl and never left. She arrives at 06:00 for a trial session, feels the ice with a blade and frowns: 'It is like skating on a parking lot.' Hard to please, loyal once happy, and the only person who irons a banner.

people.name: Kev Szabo
people.home: A bungalow with a broomball net on the garage
people.job: President, Harlow Falls Broomball Club; drives a feed truck
dislikes: being asked to keep it down
people.voice: Big laugh, big heart, louder than necessary. Sells broomball like a religion: 'It's hockey for people with dignity. Also without it.'
people.bio: Kev runs the Harlow Falls Broomball Club, which rents Wednesday late ice and forgives anything except being called curling with a ball. Broomball shoes chew the ice less than skates, but the club is loud. He is Bernie's brother, Kenny's uncle and the valley's loudest laugh.

people.name: Bernie Szabo
people.home: A Kessler side-split with three microphones in the basement
people.job: Play-by-play, CKVL 1340 Valley Radio (since 1985)
likes: a goal call that peaks on the second syllable
his son Kenny's shifts (he calls them neutrally, badly)
dislikes: being asked how to pronounce Kessler
people.voice: Broadcast baritone even when ordering fries. Narrates life in play-by-play and pronounces 'Kessler' three different ways in one breath.
people.bio: Bernie has called every Kessler home game since 1985 and the Lumber Kings' games too, and the rink's PA carries him on game nights. He keeps Szabo's Valley Hockey Almanac and can tell you the 1983 BL-D scoring leader without looking. When his son Kenny scores, he calls it like a stranger did it and his voice goes up half an octave.

people.name: Kenny Szabo
people.home: A basement apartment in Millbrook with a heater that works
people.job: Grinder winger; works the counter at Maple Tire & Muffler
people.voice: Big-hearted and self-deprecating: 'I'm not good, I'm just there.' Says 'buddy' a lot and means it every time.
people.bio: Kenny is a grinder who knows he is not quite good enough and plays like it is a privilege. On the Player path he is the owner's linemate and carpool, gets cut at Senior AAA camp the year the owner makes it, signs with the Lumber Kings anyway and becomes their captain. He is the one driving Doris the night the call comes.

people.name: Bernie Ostrowski
people.home: A ranch house with the 2009 banner photo as the screen saver
people.job: Coach, Millbrook High Mallards; phys ed teacher
likes: the 2009 valley high school title (mention it)
people.voice: Gym-teacher bonhomie. Every story leads to 2009. Deflects any question about money with a pep talk.
people.bio: Coach Bernie's Mallards won the valley high school title in 2009, and the banner is the one he points at during every phone call about late payment. His team fills dead time on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons and pays sixty days late, cheerfully. He is not the other Bernie, the radio one, and gets his mail.

people.name: Stan Kubiak
people.home: A rental on Pine Street, still in boxes after four years
people.job: Head coach, Millbrook Lumber Kings
people.voice: Tired, decent, kind. Long sighs, short sentences, one good joke a week, usually on Thursday.
people.bio: Stan is a decent man out of ideas. On the Coach path he walks out at the second intermission of a 6-1 loss to Tollbridge in Year 2 and hands the owner his whistle. He comes back later as a scout who wants to help, and is better at it.

people.name: Gary Pruett
people.home: A split-level with a backyard rink he floods badly
people.job: Manager, Valley Foods; captain of the Wobbly Pops
likes: stopping, preferably in front of the bench
being the learn-to-skate pamphlet's success story
the idea of an award named after him
dislikes: nine-year-olds who are better than him
people.voice: Proud beginner energy; every sentence is an achievement. 'Did you see me stop? I stopped.'
people.bio: Gary learned to skate the same winter his son did and refused to be outdone by a nine-year-old. He learned to stop last February and now does it at every opportunity, preferably in front of the bench. He captains the Wobbly Pops, dads with more spirit than edges.

people.name: Dr. Lyle Haverkamp
people.home: A modern house with a molar-shaped mailbox
people.job: Dentist, Haverkamp Family Dentistry; Millbrook Molars defence
likes: the unpaid invoice for Rick Saucier's tooth
passing, because nobody wants to get hit in the hands
dislikes: sugar at the Hot Stove (he buys it anyway)
people.voice: Chirpy lecturer; turns every chat into a flossing reminder. Says 'Open wide!' as a greeting and 'Rinse!' as goodbye.
people.bio: Dr. Haverkamp owns the Millbrook Molars: four dentists, a hygienist and two patients who could not say no. He lectures everyone about mouthguards and has never once worn one. He fixed Rick Saucier's tooth the morning after the Toothbrush Incident and sent the bill, and the Molars bring it to every game.

people.name: Rick "Sauce" Saucier
people.home: A house on Legion Road with the 1994 team photo in the front window
people.job: Sells farm equipment; Moose Knuckles right wing; hockey dad
likes: his son on the power play
the front row of the glass
people.voice: Loud and nostalgic; sentences start in 1994. Tender for a second when he forgets to perform, then louder to cover it.
people.bio: Sauce scored 61 goals for the 1994 Millbrook Midget AA team and has told 61 stories about it since. He plays for the Moose Knuckles, the same team back together, and is gassed by the second period. From the glass at his son's games he yells everything he wishes someone had yelled for him, which is the problem.

people.name: Dwayne Kuzyk
people.home: An apartment above the Hat Trick Tavern, which is convenient
people.job: Bartender, Hat Trick Tavern; social convenor, Ice Holes
likes: a team photo with everyone in it
people.voice: Party host; toasts everything and knows everyone's drink. Has missed eleven games and never a postgame.

schedule.doing: behind the bar at the Hat Trick

people.bio: The Ice Holes play for the postgame: the pitcher is pre-ordered for 10:45 and the hockey is in the way. Dwayne is their social convenor and the reason seat F-2-12 has a plaque. He plays broomball on Wednesdays because, he says, nobody has to pretend.

people.name: Morley Gilchrist III
people.home: Above Gilchrist & Sons Funeral Home, which he would rather not discuss at dinner
people.job: Funeral director; Pallbearers goalie
dislikes: being asked for a 'friends and family rate'
people.voice: Soft, exact and sympathetic; speaks as if consoling you about the score. Nobody can tell if he is joking. He is.
people.bio: The Pallbearers are quiet, punctual and unfailingly polite, and they arrive in the second hearse. Morley is the steadiest goalie in the valley, which he says comes with the job; nobody asks which part. He is the only beer leaguer who has ever complimented Doreen's dirge.

people.name: Colin Nolan
people.home: A tidy townhouse with a label maker
people.job: Branch manager, Frostbank Millbrook; coach of the Frozen Assets
dislikes: being asked about the line of credit at parties
people.voice: Bank-manager calm. Frames hockey as risk and return: 'That shift was an unsecured loan.'
people.bio: Colin coaches the Frozen Assets, a bench of tellers who protect a one-goal lead like an overdraft, and charges a late fee for missed shifts. He is the owner's first rival coach and later a friend who lends the spreadsheet template; it is very good. He also manages the branch that holds the rink's line of credit, which makes the handshake line complicated.

people.name: Gino Russo Jr.
people.home: Behind Puckhead Pizza
people.job: Night manager, Puckhead Pizza; Puckheads goalie
likes: his mask painted like a pepperoni puck
delivering to the rink between periods
a slice deal at the Hot Stove
people.voice: Fast, warm and salesy, always mid-delivery. Counts time in periods: 'Back in under two.'
people.bio: The Puckheads are this season's expansion team: delivery drivers who signed up on a dare, half of them in borrowed skates. Gino plays goal in a pepperoni mask and has delivered to the rink between periods, which the league has asked him to stop. His pizza is on the Hot Stove menu 'when Gino's here'.

people.name: Larry Piche
people.home: A bungalow on the plough route, so he is first out
people.job: Town snowplough driver; captain, Millbrook Mallards (beer league)
likes: writing to the Puckworth Cup trustees (twenty-one follow-ups)
a plough route done by 6 am
the Mallards' dinner off THE TABLE
dislikes: people who say the trustees will never reply
people.voice: Polite, optimistic and formal, like a letter: 'Further to my previous remarks...' Takes no reply as encouragement.
people.bio: During the 2005 lockout Larry wrote to the Puckworth Cup trustees in his neat hand and asked them to consider the Millbrook Mallards, and the Cup came to Millbrook for a night. He has sent a polite follow-up every March since and has never received a reply, which he considers encouraging. In Year 5, a reply arrives.

people.name: Tyler Brandt
people.home: A condo in the new build by the highway, with his Junior B jersey framed
people.job: Sells phones at the Harlow Falls mall; captain, Cold Ones
likes: music on a speaker in warm-up
the Senior camp invite he is sure is coming
people.voice: Cocky and energetic, sentences full of 'when I was in Junior B'. Underneath, scared. Softens in the handshake line.
people.bio: Tyler played half a season of Junior B in 2017 and brings it up in every handshake line. He is sure he is one call from Senior, and gets the call first, makes the Kessler Millmen a year ahead of the owner, struggles and comes back down. A few seasons on he is humbler and genuinely useful, and the arc lands in a handshake.

people.name: Gordon "Big Gord" Halvorsen
people.home: A ranch house behind the truck lot, with a billboard in the yard
people.job: Owner, Big Gord's Trucks (since 1977); Big Gord's Haulers defence
likes: every power play (he is on all of them)
being Santa at Skate with Santa
people.voice: SHOUTS. Everything is an advert: 'BIG GORD WON'T LET YOU WALK!' Underneath, generous to a fault and a soft touch for kids.
people.bio: Big Gord has sold trucks from the same lot outside Kessler since 1977 and stars in every advert, shouting from a truck bed. He owns the Haulers, picks the lines and insists on being on the ice for every power play. Every second Saturday of December he arrives on Doris as Santa, shouting 'Ho ho ho, Big Gord won't let you walk!' from the snow tank.

people.name: Shauna Reid
people.home: A basement suite near Harlow Falls General
people.job: Night nurse; Night Owls centre
likes: being the fastest skater in the division
dislikes: people who say 'you must be tired'
the ref room smelling of brooms
people.voice: Fast, calm, triage tone; checks on you before you notice you are hurt. 'You're fine. Ice it. Next.'
people.bio: The Night Owls are overnight bakers, two night nurses and a hospital porter, and at 11:15 pm they are wide awake when nobody else is. Shauna is the fastest skater in the division and plays every shift like a code blue. She brings day-old crullers for the refs, and every page of the incident book thanks her.

people.name: Marion Fischer
people.home: A Kessler house with more books than walls
people.job: Head librarian, Kessler Public Library; Kessler Overdues defence
likes: a hit along the boards and a whispered 'shhh'
dislikes: people who dog-ear the Dickens in the penalty box
people.voice: Whisper-quiet and pin-sharp. 'Shhh.' Then the hit.
people.bio: The Kessler Overdues are librarians: polite off the ice and the dirtiest team in the valley on it. Marion has never issued a fine she did not collect, on or off the ice. She restocks the penalty box library on her own time and has opinions about the three copies of Moose Knows.

people.name: Owen Pruett
people.home: The split-level with the bad backyard rink
people.job: Grade 5; U11 winger
likes: beating his dad at backwards crossovers
dislikes: his dad stopping in front of the bench
people.voice: Kid bluntness, slightly embarrassed by his dad. Trades trivia like currency.
people.bio: Owen learned to skate the same winter as his dad and passed him in a fortnight. He plays U11 and keeps his dad's stopping highlights to himself. He is no relation to the Pruitts and is tired of saying so.

people.name: Mason "Little Sauce" Saucier
people.home: The house on Legion Road with the 1994 photo in the window
people.job: Grade 7; U13 centre (the Sawdust)
likes: skating alone at stick and puck
drawing in the back of his school planner
people.voice: Quiet and guarded, very funny when he forgets his dad is listening. Answers 'fine' until you ask about something that is not hockey.
people.bio: Little Sauce is better than anyone his age in Millbrook and has more pressure on him than anyone his age should. His arc is about whether he still likes hockey; the answer depends on ice time, rapport and how the coach handles his dad. If it goes badly he transfers to Harlow Falls, which is a soft loss and never a disaster.

people.name: Maddie Pruitt
people.home: The Pruitt place on Birch Street
people.job: Grade 4; learn-to-skate (holds the chair)
dislikes: big kids zooming at public skate
being told it's fine when it isn't
people.voice: Small and serious; asks 'why' about physics. Says 'I'm going to fall' and then, sometimes, doesn't.
people.bio: Maddie is Dylan's little sister and the great-granddaughter of Dorothy Pruitt, who founded Honest Hockey. In week two of learn-to-skate she cannot stand; by Christmas she lets go of the chair at the Snowflake Showcase. On the Coach path she becomes the slowest skater on the U11s, the only one who listens, and in Year 3 the scorer of a tournament winner.

people.name: Carla Pruitt
people.home: The Pruitt place on Birch Street
people.job: Shift supervisor, Millbrook Dairy plant
likes: Maddie letting go of the chair
her grandmother's Honest Hockey gear (it's fine)
the radiant heaters over the east benches
dislikes: being asked if she is related to Gary (no)
Dylan's report card arriving before Dylan
people.voice: Tired, dry and fiercely loving; practical sentences and a mother's sarcasm. 'It's fine. It'll do the job.'
people.bio: Carla is Dorothy Pruitt's granddaughter, which means she was raised on gear that says exactly what it is. She raises Dylan and Maddie on early shifts at the Dairy plant and bench coffee. She is the nervous parent at learn-to-skate, and the proudest one at the Snowflake Showcase.

people.name: Tommy Bellweather
people.home: A semi on Rink Road, three doors from Old Pete
people.job: Grade 6; rink rat; runs the crest-trading table like a bank
likes: tournament pins (he is one trade from the rarest in the valley)
stick and puck at any hour
knowing where every lost puck went
people.voice: Breathless and businesslike, a fountain of facts and offers. Ends every sentence with 'right?' Quotes exchange rates in pins.
people.bio: Tommy lives at the rink in every way except the sleeping. He runs the tournament crest-trading table like a bank and is one Millbrook host pin from the rarest pin in the valley, and when the Dukes practise he stands at the glass with a puck and a pen, aiming for twelve signatures. Dylan is his hero, which Dylan finds both flattering and a lot.

people.name: Marisol Bautista
people.home: The Bautistas' duplex on Second Street
people.job: Personal support worker; adult learn-to-skate student
likes: the glide (she found it in week 3)
hot chocolate with the missing letters
dislikes: falling in front of the Mallards
people who call her brave (she is just cold)
people.voice: Warm, teasing and determined. Switches to Tagalog when she nearly falls and laughs when she does.
people.bio: Marisol grew up in Manila and never had the chance to skate, and decided at forty-two that her daughter should not be the only one in the family who can. She signs up for adult learn-to-skate on Monday nights and found the glide in week three. She watches every one of Josie's games with a thermos and her hands over her eyes.

people.name: Colette Beaulieu
people.home: The room above the bakery on Main Street
people.job: Assistant coach, Millbrook Figure Skating Club; kids' learn-to-skate; substitute teacher
dislikes: the triple loop she never landed
people.voice: Bright and encouraging, real warmth under the coach-speak: 'Knees soft, eyes up, you've got this.' Switches to French with Hélène.
people.bio: Colette skated for Hélène from age six and never landed the triple loop, which she has made peace with most days. She teaches the kids' group at learn-to-skate while Penny Marchetti takes the adults, and runs the little ones' Snowflake Showcase. Every skater in the valley under twelve calls her Coach Colette.

people.name: Josée Thibodeau
people.home: The Thibodeau house on Church Street
people.job: Grade 9; Senior Bronze skater testing her freeskate; the club's best jumper
likes: skating to music nobody else likes
dislikes: the horn going off during her run-through
people.voice: Earnest and dramatic; counts under her breath, then narrates her own disasters like an opera. 'I have DIED. Again, please.'
people.bio: Josée is the best jumper the club has had in a decade and is testing her Senior Bronze freeskate on Millbrook ice; she wants it fresh, flat and fair. She lands everything at 06:00 with nobody watching and narrates every fall like the end of an opera. A rut at the takeoff of her double axel is the fastest way to lose the figure club.

people.name: Carol Thibodeau
people.home: The Thibodeau house on Church Street
people.job: Pharmacist, Millbrook Drugs; eight years on the six a.m. coffee bench
likes: the warm corner of the east benches
dislikes: the coffee machine's NOT WORKING sign
ice that costs her daughter a jump
hockey parents in the lobby at 8
people.voice: Polite, precise, over-caffeinated. Asks about ice temperature as if it were a prescription.
people.bio: Carol has driven Josée to 06:00 ice three mornings a week for eight years and sits on the coffee bench with half the heaters working and no coffee until seven. She knows the club's competition calendar better than the club does. She and Paolo Marchetti have fought a silent war over the best filming spot on the glass since September.

people.name: Lily Marchetti
people.home: Above Marchetti's Shoe Repair
people.job: Grade 3; Star 2 skater; falls a lot, on purpose and otherwise
people.voice: Giggly and unstoppable; narrates her own routines. 'And now the princess falls DOWN.'
people.bio: Lily falls more than any skater in the club and enjoys it more than any skater in the club. She graduated from learn-to-skate a year ago and still drops in to show Maddie how to fall properly: knees bent, hands out, then laugh. Hélène says she has 'a gift for momentum'.

people.name: Paolo Marchetti
people.home: Above Marchetti's Shoe Repair on Main Street
people.job: Shoe repair (and skate-boot stretching, which annoys Bev)
likes: filming every practice from three angles
a music cue landing on time
people.voice: Excitable hand-talker who narrates his daughter like a broadcast. Bernie Szabo, but for figure skating.
people.bio: Paolo films every one of Lily's practices from three angles and edits them with music on Sunday nights. He stretches skate boots in his shoe repair, which Bev regards as a hostile act. He is the loudest person at any figure event and the first to cry.

people.name: Noah Delisle
people.home: A farmhouse on the Kessler road
people.job: Grade 11; Senior Bronze figure skater; Mallards fourth-line winger
likes: edges (he is the best skater on the Mallards and they know it)
his figure blades and his hockey blades
being the only boy in the club, mostly
dislikes: jokes about figure skating (he has replies ready)
people.voice: Easygoing and unbothered; has heard every joke. Disarms with 'Can you do a spiral? No? Then hush.'
people.bio: Noah started figure skating because his older sister did and kept going because he was good at it. He plays fourth-line wing for the Mallards and is the fastest skater on the team by a distance nobody likes to discuss. One day he will have to choose, and Hélène and Coach Bernie are both quietly campaigning.

people.name: Yvette Lacombe
people.home: A stone house in Sainte-Odile, two hours by the valley road
people.job: Figure skating judge and test evaluator
likes: a blanket in the judges' box
skaters who bow to the panel
Hélène's students (she will not say so)
dislikes: parents who argue scores in the parking lot
people.voice: Formal, exact and gently terrifying. Gives marks out loud for things that are not skating: 'The coffee, a 4.2.'
people.bio: Madame Lacombe has judged figure skating tests across the north for forty years and drives two hours to Millbrook for test day with her own blanket. She coached Hélène's coach. A cold judges' box costs the rink more than any bad ice, because she remembers.

people.name: Irene Dubois
people.home: The seniors' apartments on Church Street
people.job: Retired switchboard operator; every week at public skate since opening night, 1974
likes: public skate, every week since 2 November 1974
skating Albert's laps as well as her own
the first lap on fresh ice
dislikes: kids on phones in the lane
music too loud to count waltz time
people.voice: Courtly and old-fashioned; takes your arm before you offer it. Tells you the temperature and how the ice compares to 1974.
people.bio: Irene has skated at Millbrook every week since opening night, 2 November 1974, first with her husband Albert and, since he died, doing his laps as well as hers. She arrives early enough to watch the end of figure practice and leaves exactly when the hot chocolate is gone. For her anniversary lap she would like the Skaters' Waltz, and Doreen's Casio knows it.

people.name: Jess Whitehorse
people.home: A rented farmhouse on the Port Ainsley road
people.job: Veterinary technician, part-time
likes: Friday public skate when it is quiet
the pond at Port Ainsley in February
a dry bench for the snowsuit change
dislikes: teen boys racing through the toddler zone
the washroom with no changing table
wet ice that soaks a snowsuit
people.voice: Calm, funny, tired-mum honesty. Narrates to Birdie in the third person: 'Birdie is going to say hi. Birdie is not going to lick the glass.'
people.bio: Jess grew up skating on the lake at Port Ainsley and wants Birdie to have the same winters. She comes to Friday public skate because it is the quietest, and stays because Irene waltzes with Birdie at two miles an hour. She would like a changing table in the washroom and will mention it.

people.name: Birdie Whitehorse
people.home: The farmhouse on the Port Ainsley road
people.job: Toddler; professional faller
people.voice: One word at a time, at full volume: 'DOWIS!' 'Again!' 'Bird!'
people.bio: Birdie is three, wears a snowsuit she despises and loves Doris more than anyone in the building except Earl. She falls down every four seconds at public skate, on purpose about half the time. Earl pretends not to wave at her from the driver's seat.

people.name: Hank Lavoie
people.home: A trailer on the Kessler road with blackout curtains
people.job: Paper machine tender, nights, Kessler Pulp & Paper
likes: stick and puck at dawn, straight off the night shift
the hiss of the paper machine, oddly
dislikes: people who talk at stick and puck
people.voice: Laconic mill-worker humour; a single 'Yup' carries three paragraphs. Shoots pucks to get sleepy.
people.bio: Hank runs a paper machine on nights at Kessler Pulp & Paper, comes off at five and wants an hour of stick and puck before he sleeps. He skates in silence, shoots a hundred pucks and goes home with the sun coming up. On Wednesdays he sits in the stands for broomball and laughs once, loudly, at something nobody else saw.

people.name: Marcel Thibodeau
people.home: The Thibodeau house on Church Street, with a striped mailbox
people.job: Referee, Valley Beer League and NSHA (thirty seasons); Kessler Public Works
likes: a game nobody remembers the ref of
Rule 6.2, which he knows better than the Sin Bin Brewers
dislikes: the ref room smelling of brooms
people.voice: Unflappable and dry, a man who has heard it all and noted it in the incident book. 'Noted.'
people.bio: Marcel has refereed thirty seasons of valley hockey and written most of the incident book. He is Josée's dad and Carol's husband, and the only person in the family who thinks a 6 am alarm is a reasonable time to be at a rink. He watches his daughter's test from the lobby because he cannot bear it.

people.name: Nell Haraldsen
people.home: A Harlow Falls apartment with three whistles on the key rack
people.job: Referee, Valley Beer League (four nights a week); NSHA linesperson on Saturdays
likes: a second coat hook in the ref room
figure shows on her nights off
a game nobody remembers the ref of
dislikes: the roof drip on the home blue line
the ref room smelling of brooms
people.voice: Sharp, warm and organised; explains offside to anyone, unprompted, with diagrams on napkins. Asks politely, twice, then writes it in the book.
people.bio: Nell referees the Valley Beer League four nights a week and works the lines in the NSHA on Saturdays, and intends to be the first woman to referee in the ILHL. The ref room is a former broom closet with one coat hook for three officials, and the incident book has asked politely for a second in her handwriting. On her nights off she watches figure shows, for the edges.

people.name: Brody Sauvé
people.home: His parents' house behind the curling club
people.job: Grade 10; minor hockey referee (Level 1)
likes: his whistle with no tooth marks (yet)
dislikes: the cold in the ref room
people.voice: Nervous, earnest rule-quoter; his voice cracks on the big calls. Tougher than he looks.
people.bio: Brody refs minor hockey on weekends for $25 a game and the experience. He is fifteen, polite, right about the rules and yelled at by grown men who are wrong about them. Marcel has told him the yelling gets quieter; Marcel is lying, kindly.

people.name: Moose Kowalczuk
people.home: A house in Kingsport full of paperbacks and loud plaid
people.job: Host, Moose on the Loose (Saturday Night Hockey); summer hockey school
likes: mystery novels (the butler didn't do it)
people.voice: Gentle giant, soft-spoken and bookish, with television warmth. Ends advice with 'Moose knows.'
people.bio: Moose holds the all-time penalty minutes record, by a distance the league calls 'an era', and never hit anyone from behind. In 1984 he served 17 minutes in the Millbrook penalty box at an exhibition and left a paperback, which started the penalty box library. He runs a summer hockey school that could rent Millbrook ice, if the ice is in by August.

people.name: Barry "Suitcase" Pomeroy
people.home: A Duncannon house with a packed suitcase by the door, still
people.job: Retired GNHL defenceman; Duncannon Dukes community ambassador
likes: standing ovations on arrival and departure
bringing a suitcase to the rink, just in case
people.voice: Cheerful, self-deprecating journeyman. Every story ends with him being traded: 'And then I was in Fairhaven.'
people.bio: Suitcase played for nine GNHL clubs and was sent down to the Duncannon Dukes seven times; the Duncannon fans gave him a standing ovation every time he arrived and every time he left. He won his only Cup in his final game. Now he skates with the Dukes at practice as their ambassador and visits the Haverstock Old-timers' the year the owner turns 30.

people.name: Donnie Delorme
people.home: Above Delorme's Bakery, Harlow Falls
people.job: Baker (the better twin)
likes: beer league hockey from the back row
a well-run power play, from a distance
people.voice: Says almost nothing; communicates in baked goods. A cake that says 'NO' is a complete sentence.
people.bio: In 1996 Donnie played eleven GNHL games in place of his twin Ricky and played better; he was caught signing an autograph with his own name. Three teams offered him contracts and he went back to his bakery. He sits in the back row at beer league games, and sometimes, at dawn stick and puck, does something with a puck that makes Hank Lavoie stop shooting.

people.name: Hap Doyle
people.home: A Kessler farmhouse within earshot of the mill whistle
people.job: Head coach, Kessler Millmen (since 1988)
likes: his practice plans (DO NOT REMOVE FROM KESSLER)
people.voice: Monosyllabic. 'We'll see.' Silence is his paragraph.
people.bio: Hap has coached the Kessler Millmen since 1988 and smiled once, in 1996; the photo hangs in the Barn with a card that says HE DENIES IT. He comes to Millbrook with the Millmen and leaves his practice plans in the visitors' room more often than a careful man should. His arc ends, on any path, with the second smile in recorded history.

people.name: Annette Rourke
people.home: A Duncannon condo with a freezer full of ice cups
people.job: Head coach, Duncannon Dukes (CHA)
likes: a player who is the same every night
a cup of ice to chew
10 am practice ice when the Frostbank Centre has a concert
people.voice: Fair, cold and fast; short declaratives. 'I don't need you to be good. I need you to be the same every night.'
people.bio: Annette played defence in the CHA and now coaches the Dukes, chewing ice from a cup behind the bench. She books Millbrook practice ice on Mondays and Wednesdays when the Frostbank Centre has concerts, and only if the ice is 85 or better. She measures it herself.

people.name: Merv Tolliver
people.home: A Duncannon apartment with a typewriter he is rude to
people.job: Columnist, The Last Word, The Duncannon Daily Ledger
likes: a crowd that knows every player's mother
people.voice: Acid, elegant and secretly sentimental. Speaks in column ledes: 'I drove forty minutes so you don't have to.'
people.bio: Merv writes The Last Word for the valley's only daily and hates everything, which is how you know you have arrived. He drives to Millbrook once the Lumber Kings host a game the Ledger covers and reviews the rink in stars. His review reruns with new text as the rooms are renovated, and he always comes back.

people.name: Cody Lindqvist
people.home: An apartment over the Sin Bin Brewpub, Harlow Falls
people.job: Brewmaster, Sin Bin Brewpub; Sin Bin Brewers defence
likes: beers named after penalties (he has earned all of them)
dislikes: his mum reading the penalty sheet
people.voice: Rules-lawyer charm; quotes the rulebook with a brewer's patience and a defenceman's timing. 'Technically...'
people.bio: Cody leads the C Division in penalty minutes, almost all of them for explaining the rulebook to referees. He is usually right and gets two minutes anyway, for the tone. His mother, Marg, reads the penalty sheet every week and annotates it in red.

people.name: Penny Marchetti
people.home: A flat over the bakery on Main Street, next door to Colette
people.job: Gym teacher, Millbrook Elementary; adult learn-to-skate instructor
likes: skate aids made from broken sticks
a gym class that ends with nobody crying
dislikes: her brother's camera at her classes
people.voice: Cheerful and practical, a gym teacher's voice that carries without shouting. 'Right! Hands on knees, eyes up, and we march like penguins.'
people.bio: Penny teaches gym at Millbrook Elementary and the adult learn-to-skate on Monday nights, where there are more beginners than boards. She wants skate aids for grown-ups and thinks the broken-stick barrel and Lorne Pettipiece could make them. She is Paolo's younger sister and Lily's favourite person on the ice.

people.name: Walter Oduya
people.home: A brick house in Kessler with his granddaughter's drawings on the fridge
people.job: Retired electrician, Kessler Pulp & Paper; adult learn-to-skate student
people.voice: Gentle, methodical, an electrician's patience. Treats every fall like a fault to trace: 'Right. Left foot. That's where the trouble is.'
people.bio: Walter wired half of Kessler Pulp & Paper over thirty-five years and has never once been on skates. His granddaughter Zuri, six, skates like a sparrow, and he would like to do one lap with her at public skate before she decides grandpas can't. He comes to Monday learn-to-skate in a helmet and takes notes.

people.name: Devon Marsh
people.home: An apartment in Harlow Falls with two pairs of skates by the door
people.job: Line cook, the Slapshot Saloon
likes: Saturday public skate, where they met
people.voice: Earnest and nervous; rehearsed lines that go charmingly wrong. Checks his coat pocket every ninety seconds.
people.bio: Devon met Ama at Saturday public skate, when she skated into him and apologised to the boards. He wants to propose to her there, during their song, with the lights down, and needs a plan, a song and a dimmer. He has told everyone except Ama.

people.name: Rhonda Pelkey
people.home: A Harlow Falls duplex with a gold rubber boot on the porch
people.job: Hydro dispatcher; Harlow Falls Broomball Club goalie
likes: the Golden Boot (a rubber boot painted gold)
dislikes: skaters who call it 'curling with a ball'
the Golden Boot living on her porch
people.voice: Loud, quick and very funny, a dispatcher's calm in the crease. Has a nickname for everyone within one meeting.
people.bio: Rhonda keeps goal for the Harlow Falls Broomball Club and keeps the Golden Boot, the Winter Carnival trophy, on her porch, because nobody has given it a better home. She would like ice for the Carnival final that won't eat sneakers. She and Earl disagree about when the flood should happen, every Wednesday.

people.name: Lisa Cormier
people.home: A bungalow on Birch Street with a muffin tin always in use
people.job: Dental hygienist; U7 novice team manager
likes: public skate with the whole team
dislikes: the visitors' room at 8 am in January
parents who leave before the skates are off
people.voice: Cheerful and frazzled, talks in lists, offers you a muffin as punctuation.
people.bio: Lisa manages the U7 novice team: fifteen five-year-olds, thirty mittens and one visitors' room at eight on Saturdays where nobody can do up skates with frozen fingers. She panic-bakes blueberry muffins before every game. She works for Dr. Haverkamp and is the only person who has ever made him wear a mouthguard, once.

people.name: Desmond Faulk
people.home: A house on Elm Street with a sousaphone in the hall
people.job: Music teacher, Millbrook High; leads the pep band
likes: a pep band that plays in tune, roughly
the Mallards scoring on a downbeat
dislikes: being told to keep it down
a goal during a key change
people.voice: Jovial and musical, hums the fight song between sentences; conducts with whatever he is holding.
people.bio: Desmond teaches music at Millbrook High and leads the pep band and its 1971 sousaphone. He would like the band to play Mallards games from Section C, which has no letter and which everybody calls Section See. He and Doreen have a professional rivalry conducted entirely in key changes.

people.name: Bob Ferreira
people.home: A tidy house by the old station with a timetable on the fridge
people.job: Retired freight dispatcher (Carrick Junction); chair, Valley Peewee Tournament committee
likes: a game every seventy-five minutes with a flood between
people.voice: Railway precision, kindly delivered; speaks in departure times. 'Game four departs at 10:45. Not 10:46.'
people.bio: Bob dispatched freight out of Carrick Junction for thirty-four years and retired to Millbrook to be near his grandkids. He chairs the Valley Peewee Tournament committee, which runs a game every seventy-five minutes with a flood between, and would like it to run on time for once in its life. He has a pocket watch and uses it.

people.name: Réjean Paquette
people.home: A Duncannon semi with an infrared gun on the dashboard of every car he has owned
people.job: Equipment manager, Duncannon Dukes (twenty-six years)
likes: numbers that agree with the log
Old Pete's sharpening, which he will not admit
people.voice: A professional frown; speaks in temperatures. 'Minus five point two. You said minus five. You were close.'
people.bio: Réjean has kept the Dukes' equipment for twenty-six years and trusts only his own infrared gun. When the Dukes practise at Millbrook he walks the ice before they skate and compares his numbers with the log, and with yours. He and Old Pete have never been in the same room without discussing hollows.

people.name: Terry Duffy
people.home: Above Duffy Bros. Plumbing & Heating
people.job: Plumber, Duffy Bros. Plumbing & Heating; Plungers centre
likes: his pager (he says he hates it)
dislikes: his pager going off on a breakaway
people who say 'number two business' like they thought of it
people.voice: Matter-of-fact tradesman humour; every problem is a clog with a cause.
people.bio: Terry centres the Plungers, the best-organised team in C until someone gets an emergency call mid-game. He still carries a pager, and it goes off about once a game, usually on a breakaway; the refs rule it a line change. Washroom 2 is, professionally, his favourite and least favourite room in the building.

people.name: Lorne Pettipiece
people.home: A workshop with a house attached, outside Harlow Falls
people.job: Woodworker, Pettipiece Woodworks
likes: a bench made of forty-one Warlocks
dislikes: people who sit on his benches before they're dry
people.voice: Unhurried, sawdust-dry humour; measures twice and talks once.
people.bio: Lorne buys broken sticks from Bev's barrel, three dollars for wood and a dollar for composite, and turns them into coat racks, benches and the odd Adirondack chair. The Warlock bench by the front doors is his, built from forty-one broken Warlocks. Bev says it is sturdier than they ever were as sticks.
